title: Capture the opening number before kickoff, every week
evidence: The store holds a closing number for 136 games and zero opening numbers. ESPN renders an open/current pair for unplayed games, so the data exists before kickoff and disappears after it.
unlocks: Closing-line value, line-movement signals, and a real test of whether our number leads or follows the market.
cost: One fixed pre-kickoff capture per week, with the timestamp stored.
risk: A capture that is not timestamped is worthless; a capture after kickoff is a leak. Both must be blocked in code.
acceptance_test: A stored open and close for the same game, with two different times, and a test that fails if open_time >= kickoff_time.

title: Fix or retire the total model before publishing it
evidence: Our total runs 3.237 points above market and correlates -0.0418 with the actual total, against 0.3771 for the market. That is the wrong sign.
unlocks: A total column that is a forecast rather than an artefact.
cost: One specification change, plus a held-out test window.
risk: Fixing it on the graded weeks turns 136 games into a fitted curve and destroys the only clean test that exists.
acceptance_test: The corrected total is fitted on weeks 1-4 only and its correlation with weeks 5-9 outcomes is positive with n printed; if it is not, the column stays blank.

title: Add a second, independent price source and show disagreements
evidence: All prices come from one publisher. Two pages of that publisher agreeing is internal consistency, not verification.
unlocks: A defensible price, and the ability to say which number is real when they differ.
cost: One more official source read per week.
risk: A second source with a different definition (open vs close, one book vs consensus) creates false disagreements unless the definition is recorded.
acceptance_test: Both sources stored for the same game with their definitions, and a disagreement table that is non-empty when they differ.

title: Pre-register the strategy family before the next window
evidence: 12 variants were graded and none clears q<=0.1. The family was written after the data was seen, so even a pass would be weak.
unlocks: A result that means something the first time it appears.
cost: A frozen file, a commit hash, and the discipline not to edit it.
risk: A pre-registered family that nobody enforces is worse than none, because it looks rigorous.
acceptance_test: The family file's hash is committed before the first graded week and the build fails if it changes.

title: Make the demotion gate fire on real history before trusting it
evidence: 8 of 12 variants are in demote_to_paper, but only on paper. The gate has never seen a live promotion.
unlocks: A gate whose false-positive and false-negative rates are known.
cost: Replay across prior seasons where full data exists.
risk: A gate tuned until it never fires protects nothing.
acceptance_test: Replay a season with a known regime change and show the gate fires within the stated window, with the firing date recorded.

title: Capture a depth chart every week, not once
evidence: One week of charts covers 31 clubs and 265 matched injury rows. With one week there is no variation, so 'deep' versus 'thin' cannot be tested against results.
unlocks: A testable injury term, and the ability to price a depletion.
cost: 32 club pages per week, each with its own rendering quirks.
risk: Club charts are published on inconsistent dates and are sometimes unofficial; a stale chart silently becomes a wrong depth.
acceptance_test: The same club's chart captured in two consecutive weeks, with the printed date recorded on each and any change listed.

title: Publish a per-row 'why this is blank' reason code
evidence: Blank cells already carry a rule, but the reader cannot tell 'no source exists' from 'source exists and was not captured' from 'captured and withheld for rights'.
unlocks: A reviewer can triage gaps instead of investigating each one.
risk: A reason code can become a hiding place if it is never audited.
acceptance_test: Every blank cell has a code from a closed list, and a count per code is published.

title: State the price assumption on every screen that shows a unit total
evidence: Every staking number is at an assumed -110, and the store holds no price at all. The leaderboard says so; a screenshot or a copied table would not.
unlocks: A number that cannot be mistaken for a profit claim.
cost: A caption that travels with the value.
acceptance_test: A test that fails if a units column renders without its assumption string in the same table.
